summary: Mark McClish is an indology and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate under Patrick Olivelle. In 2012, he was affiliated with Birmingham-Southern College and served on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies.
Mark Owen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Leeds under doctoral supervisors Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (1951–2025) was an Indologist. He earned degrees at Banaras Hindu University, a PhD at Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson (~1975–1979), and a DLitt at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1985), studying under various traditional teachers.

Mark Siderits (born 1946) is a philosopher specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Illinois State University (~1979–2008) and Seoul National University (~2008–2012), holding the title of Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at both institutions.

Mark Singleton is an indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge and studied under Elizabeth De Michelis and Lakshmi Tatacharya. In 2020, he was a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London.

Mark T. Unno works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1977–1981) and Stanford University (~1987–1994), later holding posts at Brown University (~1994–1998) and the University of Oregon (~2000).

Mark Tatz (1946–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz by 1978, studied with several traditional teachers, and was a professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies (1988).

Mark Teeuwen (born 1966) is a Japanologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his MA (~1984–1989) and PhD (~1989–1996) at Leiden University, lectured at Cardiff University (1994–1999), and became Professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.

Markus Gabriel (born 1980) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn (~2002–2005). He has held posts at Bonn (~2009), UC Berkeley, The New School, and the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy (2024).

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna by 2012 under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, later working as a project researcher at the University of Heidelberg.

Marsha Weidner is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. She held art history posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Marshall Sahlins (1930–2021) was an anthropologist and historian. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1947–1952) and Columbia University (~1952–1954), later holding posts at the University of Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago (from 1973).

Martha Nussbaum (born 1947) is a philosopher educated at Wellesley, NYU, and Harvard. After teaching at Harvard, Oxford, and Brown, she joined the University of Chicago faculty in 1995 as Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor of Law and Ethics.

Martin Baumann (born 1960) is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his PhD at Leibniz University Hannover (~1989–1993) and habilitated at Leipzig (~1994–1999) before becoming Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

Martin Brauen (born 1948) is a Tibetologist and historian who studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Zurich. He held long-term posts at the University of Zurich's Ethnographic Museum (1975) and the Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

Martin Collcutt (born 1939) is a historian specializing in Japanology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge and Harvard (PhD 1975), he taught at Yokohama National University and the University of Tokyo before serving as professor at Princeton University (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen by 2002. He held research positions at Hamburg, Göttingen, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Ryukoku University.

Martin Haug (1827–1876) studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn. He served as Privatdozent at Bonn, held the Professorship of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1859–1866), and was later Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at the University of Munich (1868).

Martin Heidegger (1889–1976) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert and Edmund Husserl. He held teaching posts at the University of Marburg (1923–1928) and the University of Freiburg (1915–1923; 1928–1958).

Martin Joachim Kümmel (born 1970) is a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian-Central Asian studies scholar. Educated at the University of Freiburg (PhD 1998, Habilitation 2005), he worked at Freiburg (~2003–2011) and became a chairholder at the University of Jena in 2013.
